name: New Mexico
agency: New Mexico Energy, Minerals and Natural Resources Department, State Parks Division

rule.textEn: Anyone born on or after Jan. 1, 1989 needs a New Mexico boater education card on board to run any motorboat, PWC or undocumented sailboat.
rule.textEs: Quien nació el 1 de enero de 1989 o después debe llevar a bordo la tarjeta de educación náutica de Nuevo México para manejar cualquier lancha, moto acuática o velero no documentado.

exemptions: Holders of a valid U.S. Coast Guard marine operator license.
Non-residents with a NASBLA-standard card from another state or country.
Renters (30 days or less) briefed by the rental agent with a signed checklist.
Boat bought within the last 30 days, with the bill of sale on board.
New residents: 45 days with their out-of-state card.

card.feeNote: State park ranger and Coast Guard Auxiliary classroom courses are free; online providers set their own price.

nonResident: Visitors with a NASBLA-standard card from their home state or country are exempt; new residents have 45 days.
rental: Renters for 30 days or less may skip the card after the rental agent briefs them and they sign a safety checklist.

sources.quote: A person born on or after January 1, 1989 who operates a motorboat on the state’s waters shall possess a division-issued boater education card and have it onboard the motorboat during its operation

sources.publisher: New Mexico Administrative Code 18.17.4 NMAC (State Records Center and Archives)
sources.quote: motorboat includes any vessel propelled or designed to be propelled by sail and that does not have a valid document issued by a federal agency, but does not include a sailboard or windsurf board.

sources.publisher: New Mexico Energy, Minerals and Natural Resources Department, State Parks Division
sources.quote: The New Mexico boater education card is valid for your lifetime

sources.publisher: New Mexico Energy, Minerals and Natural Resources Department, State Parks Division
sources.quote: The fee for a replacement card is $10.

sources.publisher: New Mexico Energy, Minerals and Natural Resources Department, State Parks Division
sources.quote: You are not a New Mexico resident and hold a valid boater education card from another state.

sources.publisher: New Mexico Energy, Minerals and Natural Resources Department, State Parks Division
sources.quote: You are renting a boat and have received safety instructions and have completed a dockside safety checklist provided by the rental agent.

sources.publisher: New Mexico Energy, Minerals and Natural Resources Department, State Parks Division
sources.quote: You have moved to New Mexico from another state and can show a valid boater education card from another state. After 45 days you must have a New Mexico boater education card.
